narrative.overview: InsightForge is a dark-adapted instrument. Its job is to make three hard-to-see things visible in one sitting: the passage inside a paper that actually answers the question, the row that does not belong in a dataset, and the count that contradicts the narrative. The surface stays dark so the content carries the light. There is one signal colour — a sodium yellow that reads as an instrument lamp — and it is spent narrowly: on the action you came to take, the thing you have selected, and the state of the system. The palette is deliberately two-material. A near-black canvas holds glass panels built from white at 2–4.5% opacity, separated by 1px hairlines. Nothing in the neutral layer carries hue, which is what lets a saturated yellow survive without shouting. The accent is not hardcoded: it lives in index.css as --accent, --accent-light, --on-accent, --accent-soft and --accent-glow, exposed as Tailwind theme colours and CSS variables, with theme.js mirroring them for Plotly.
keyCharacteristics: One dark canvas (#04070a); depth comes from white-alpha glass, never from a second background family.
A single accent, yellow (#fdc500), reserved for action, selection, focus and status.
The accent appears as a light-to-dark gradient under near-black ink; never as a solid fill behind light text.
1px white-alpha hairlines do the work shadows usually do; the primary action and the winning chart bar are the only things that glow.
Small, tracked, uppercase labels for region names; 12px floor for anything a user must read.
Tabular figures everywhere a column of numbers can appear.

rules.name: The Yellow-Is-A-State Rule
rules.body: The accent marks something the user can do, has selected, or the system is reporting. It is never a decorative accent, a background wash, or a bullet colour.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Chart Rule
rules.body: A chart uses one hue for magnitude (accent at 30–62% alpha) and rose for anomaly. Never interpolate between accent and rose across a continuous scale — the midpoint goes muddy brown.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything a user must read is at least 12px. 11px is permitted only for uppercase tracked labels and table headers.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any column of numbers gets tabular-nums. Digits that do not line up vertically are a defect.

rules.name: The Lit-Edge Rule
rules.body: A surface separates itself with a hairline or an inset highlight, never a drop shadow. Glows belong to actions and to the one bar that must win the eye.

rules.name: The No-Olive Rule
rules.body: A yellow surface at low alpha over near-black reads brown or olive. Below 12% opacity, glow and wash surfaces are drawn in white instead.

dos: Do keep the canvas at #04070a and build depth from white-alpha fills plus 1px hairlines.
Do spend the accent on action, selection, focus and status — one solid accent action per region.
Do put near-black #0a0800 ink on yellow; light text on yellow fails contrast.
Do reach for bg-accent, text-on-accent, accent/10 and ring-accent/20 rather than a hex value.
Do use dashed white/10 borders for every empty state and drop zone.
Do reach for tabular-nums on any numeric column and on the KPI readouts.
Do keep the 12px floor and use #94a3b8 / #7c8ba1 for secondary text.
Do label every figure with its source, and describe an empty state by what will appear.
Do truncate long filenames and titles with a title attribute carrying the full value.
donts: Don't reintroduce sky, indigo, slate-900, or any hued neutral surface.
Don't use yellow as a decorative fill, a background wash, or gradient text.
Don't paint a large low-alpha yellow wash; over near-black it reads olive.
Don't interpolate a colour scale between the accent and rose.
Don't colour the anomaly cut-off with a warm tone — it is #cbd5e1, dashed 6 4.
Don't use a solid rose fill larger than a chip, a bar, or an error panel.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, buttons, or the sidebar.
Don't go above 26px radius, and don't pill anything except chips, status readouts, and the landing CTAs.
Don't hide, collapse, or ellipsize a citation.
